Narrator & Maya
Read the article
A career announcement
Narrator
!-- -->For the last three months, I've been doing G T M engineering. Small career change. Same laptop. Different people disappointed in me.
Maya
!-- -->Congratulations. What do you actually do?
!-- -->I connect... things. Commercially.
!-- -->A plumber with LinkedIn.

!-- -->Please don't put that on my invoice. I used to explain why the software didn't work. Now the software works, and I explain why nobody bought anything. So the bugs have acquired purchasing authority.
!-- -->And this conversation is going to explain your new job?
!-- -->Beautifully. You'll leave knowing when to nod, when to say interesting signal, and how to mute yourself before asking what pipeline means.
!-- -->One real campaign observation. Everything else, including the travel plans, is a dramatization of a meeting that should have been stopped.
!-- -->The useful explanation is the next article. They can't make me do two jobs.
This part of the article
The explanation escapes
!-- -->G T M means go to market. You use data and software to help the right message reach the right person at a useful moment. There. That's actually most of it.
!-- -->Oh! I got it. We're done.
!-- -->No, wait. I've booked the room for an hour.
!-- -->Of course you have.

!-- -->The person belongs to an account, the account fits the I C P, the I C P has intent, intent becomes a signal, signal enters a workflow, workflow creates a task, task goes to David, David asks who this person is. Easy.
!-- -->Where did David come from?
!-- -->Don't ask that. He came bundled with the C R M.
!-- -->Is there documentation?
!-- -->There's a dashboard. It has a little loading circle. That's how you know it's thinking.
A very specific everyone
!-- -->Let me try. Ideal customer profile. We decide which companies could actually benefit from the product.
!-- -->Yes. Our imaginary product makes meetings shorter. Who has meetings?
!-- -->Everyone.
!-- -->Huge market. Write that down.
!-- -->No. We need filters. Company size, relevant problem, whether they can buy it.
!-- -->More than fifty employees. Growing team. Head of operations. Public interest in efficiency, demonstrated during a forty-minute webinar about reducing unnecessary communication.
!-- -->I attended that. There was a follow-up webinar.
!-- -->Now the spreadsheet is wider. Same companies, but you have to scroll sideways to doubt them.
!-- -->I miss the plumber.
Uncertainty gets dressed
!-- -->Next: enrichment. The spreadsheet needs vitamins. We add websites, titles, company size. Useful information, allegedly.
!-- -->This source says sixty employees. This one says two hundred.
!-- -->The website says small team, big mission. So: somewhere between sixty and a mission.
!-- -->Which number goes into the system?
!-- -->We give it a confidence score. Uncertainty puts on a tie. Everyone relaxes.
!-- -->Mine's wearing a waistcoat. Can it approve expenses?
!-- -->After enrichment, deduplication. David Smith, Dave Smith, D. Smith. We merge them. Three rows become one. Beautiful.
!-- -->Three different people.
!-- -->Ah. We'll fix that downstream.
!-- -->Where is downstream?
!-- -->Nobody knows. Excellent schools, apparently. All our problems move there.
Fourteen points for a thumb
!-- -->A signal is an event worth investigating. A new office. A relevant hire. Some context that makes a conversation timely.
!-- -->Or someone liked a post.
!-- -->They liked a post about saving time. They want efficiency. They need our product. They're practically signing.
!-- -->Their thumb slipped.
!-- -->Fourteen points.
!-- -->For an accident? Why fourteen?
!-- -->Ten sounded made up.
!-- -->What's the temperature of this extremely interested thumb?
!-- -->Fifty points: hot. Seventy: very hot. Ninety: David considers sending an email. The crowd goes... back to work, because nobody has actually spoken to a customer.
!-- -->We've built a thermometer for a conversation that hasn't happened. Can it detect embarrassment?
!-- -->Enterprise plan.
Human, according to three engineers
!-- -->Please tell me the message sounds normal.
!-- -->Hi David. Noticed you're Head of Operations at a company. As Head of Operations at a company, you probably care about operations.
!-- -->You've caught him. He's operating.
!-- -->First draft. We improve the prompt. Add context. Remove hope this finds you well. New version: David. We know about the operations.
!-- -->Come out with your workflows up.
!-- -->Put hope this finds you well back in. Immediately.
!-- -->Three engineers and a language model inspect it. They agree a human could have written it. So we send it to a human.
!-- -->Not interested.
!-- -->A reply! Engagement!
!-- -->Stop celebrating!
!-- -->Don't tell the dashboard. It's having a good day.
The actual observation

!-- -->Here's the real observation. In a LinkedIn campaign, our women business development representatives got roughly twice the connection acceptance rate of our men. Business development representatives are the people doing the outreach.
!-- -->That's a result worth looking into. Were the audiences comparable? Messages? Profiles? Timing?
!-- -->Exactly the questions you'd need. The result alone doesn't tell us why. It isn't a rule about women and men.
!-- -->Good. So what did the fictional meeting inside your head recommend?
!-- -->Thailand.
!-- -->Sorry. What?
!-- -->Next year's offsite. Thailand. Two bars on a chart. One airplane. A surprisingly short presentation.
!-- -->You haven't controlled a single variable, and you're choosing seat numbers.
!-- -->David and Sean asked what this had to do with team building. I said: everything, gentlemen. We are becoming data-driven.
!-- -->Somebody take the laser pointer away from him.
An extremely fictional offsite
!-- -->Entirely imaginary offsite. Costume party. Sunshine. A slide deck with no return ticket to common sense. David and Sean have negotiated the wardrobe budget before anyone has tested the idea.
!-- -->Their glamorous lady alter egos look incredible. The wigs. The outfits. The exact same unresolved C R M permissions.
!-- -->David wants to know if the new persona gets a higher base salary. Sean has submitted false eyelashes under sales enablement.
!-- -->Finance approved one eyelash. The other one's a stretch goal.
!-- -->No. Don't put that in the deck. They'll actually do it.
!-- -->The women on the team have a cheaper suggestion. Test the targeting. Test the message. Same people, better experiment.
!-- -->Too late. Leadership has seen the airplane. You cannot unshow an airplane.
!-- -->Everyone keeps their identity. Nobody changes anything except outfits. The joke is your business reasoning, which has somehow become the least convincing costume.
!-- -->The wigs have better methodology than the deck. I admit that. But mine has transitions.
A small problem with revenue
!-- -->Did the extra connections become useful conversations?
!-- -->We were celebrating.
!-- -->Accepted connection. Meeting. Customer. Happy customer. Different things. Someone still has to want the product.
!-- -->A dependency on the product. At this stage?
!-- -->Where are those numbers on the dashboard?
!-- -->Under Advanced. Collapsed by default. The first number is very large and green. That one's doing wonderful things for morale.
!-- -->Revenue is an advanced feature.
!-- -->We've already paid for the costumes. We're emotionally invested in the hypothesis. Finance doesn't have a column for that, which is why it's so expensive.
!-- -->Downstream has a column.
!-- -->Downstream has everything.
The doorbell architecture
!-- -->Finally. Automation. Something I recognize. A webhook is one system telling another system something happened. Like a doorbell.
!-- -->Ding dong.
!-- -->That rings another doorbell. That updates a spreadsheet. That sends a message saying the original doorbell is unavailable. Someone retries it. Now there are four doorbells.
!-- -->Ding dong!
!-- -->Please. I used to sleep. We've got rate limits, missing fields, and a timestamp arriving from tomorrow to warn us.
!-- -->A human checks the output before anything embarrassing goes out, yes?
!-- -->Yes. Even this fictional company can afford that. Signal, enrichment, score, owner, task, human review. There is a useful system in here. It's just surrounded.
!-- -->Time saved?
!-- -->Six minutes. Took an afternoon to maintain. But next week, thousands of runs. Potentially worth it. Potentially my new weekend.
!-- -->The diagram doesn't fit on my screen.
!-- -->Architecture.
One invoice, four victories
!-- -->Someone bought the meeting software!
!-- -->Sales says it was the call. Marketing says the campaign. Product says the product. I say the integration, because I've been here until eleven.
!-- -->The customer says a colleague recommended it.
!-- -->Does the colleague have an A P I?
!-- -->First touch gets credit for the first interaction. Last touch gets the last. Which are we using?
!-- -->Our fictional all-touch model. Everybody wins. Four customers from one invoice. Finally, a conversion rate that respects the team.
!-- -->One customer.
!-- -->One customer. Four departments. I connect the systems so we can see what happened. Then they disagree and I become a diplomat with A P I keys.
!-- -->You wanted a change from debugging.
!-- -->I debug the sentence this lead should have been mine. The sentence has been in production since 1998.
Certification pending
!-- -->Hang on. Find suitable companies. Understand them. Notice useful moments. Build reliable plumbing. Check whether it helped. That's the job?
!-- -->You're getting dangerously close. Let me help.
!-- -->We operationalize an intent-led, signal-enriched, multi-touch revenue motion across the entire customer lifecycle, with a human in the loop and Sean in a very good wig.
!-- -->I had it. I actually had it for a second, and now it's gone.
!-- -->Perfect. You're ready for the kickoff.
!-- -->What do I do if someone asks about revenue?
!-- -->Dashboard's refreshing.
!-- -->Thailand?
!-- -->Downstream.
!-- -->David?
!-- -->Merged with two other Davids. We're sending flowers.
!-- -->Write the useful version, please. I would read it. I might even understand what you do.
!-- -->I will. For now, three months in, one solid conclusion: test the message before booking the flight.
!-- -->Interesting signal.
Until next time
!-- -->Thanks for listening. Follow along for more articles, experiments, and things that worked on my machine.
!-- -->Some of them might even work on yours.
!-- -->No promises. Have a lovely day. Go make something.
!-- -->Preferably a cup of tea first. Bye!
